note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address and opening time below comes from the City of Lincoln's own pages — its Tennis and Pickleball page for the counts and the programming, and each park's own page in Parks A to Z for the address and the hours. Where those two City records disagree, and at two of the three venues they do, this page says so rather than picking the tidier answer. The City names a fourth park with six courts that is not published here, and the reason is at the bottom of this page.

slots.parking: Lincoln publishes nothing about parking at Ballard or Peterson, and at Densmore it publishes a number for the wrong thing: "200 parking stalls", stated in a paragraph about renting the park's four baseball fields. That is a car park serving a ballfield complex on a 61-acre site, and whether it is the one you want for the pickleball courts is not something the City says. All three parks are suburban rather than street-grid sites — Ballard out by Havelock in the north-east, Peterson off Southwood Drive in the south, Densmore south of 14th and Old Cheney — so street parking is the ordinary expectation and none of it is verified. What the City does publish, and almost no operator in this directory does, is when the gates are open: 5:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m., every day, at all three.
slots.peak_hours: There is a real answer here and it is unusual: the courts have a schedule, and somebody else owns it. The City states that "Pickleball Lincoln, Inc. organizes and schedules pickleball programming at Peterson Park, Ballard Park, Eden Park, Henry Park, Roberts Park, Densmore Park, and Seng Park at University Place", and that during the times in that programming schedule, the dual-use courts at those parks "are reserved for pickleball play". It also says the public is welcome to join in. So the busy times at these parks are not a matter of guessing at demand — they are published by an organisation, on a schedule, and the reservation only bites on the dual-use courts. At Ballard and Peterson, where every court is dedicated to pickleball, a reserved session does not take a court away from pickleball; it decides who you are playing with. At Densmore, where four of the six courts are tennis courts wearing pickleball lines, it decides whether those four are pickleball courts that afternoon at all. This site does not publish the schedule itself, because it is a separate document that changes.
slots.surface_condition: Not stated anywhere in Lincoln, which is the ordinary case — only two cities in this directory publish a surface at all. What the City does distinguish, and does clearly, is a much more useful thing: whether a court is a pickleball court or a tennis court with lines on it. Its page has a "Dedicated Pickleball Courts" section and a "Dual Striped" section, and it puts each park in one of them. Sixteen of the twenty-two courts published here are dedicated. That is the highest proportion of dedicated outdoor courts in any city on this site, and it matters more than a surface note would: on a dedicated court the net is at pickleball height and the only lines are yours.
slots.local_scene: Twenty-two verified courts across three parks, sixteen of them dedicated to pickleball. Peterson Park alone has ten, which puts it among the larger dedicated sets anywhere in this directory. The City also names a fourth park with six more dedicated courts — Eden — and seven further parks with dual-striped courts it never counts, so the real number in Lincoln is comfortably higher than twenty-two and we will not guess at it. The thing that stands out about Lincoln is not the provision but who runs play on it: an outside organisation, Pickleball Lincoln, Inc., schedules programming across seven City parks with the City's blessing, and the City publishes that arrangement on its own page. No other operator in this directory hands its courts to a named organisation and says so.

best_for.heading: Best if you want a real rotation
best_for.text: Peterson (Erwin) Park has ten courts dedicated to pickleball, the largest count in Lincoln and the only venue in the city the City counts twice — once on its pickleball page and once on the park's own page. Open 5:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. daily. Ten dedicated courts is enough that a scheduled session and a casual game can happen at the same time.

best_for.heading: Best if you are tired of tennis lines
best_for.text: Ballard Park's six courts are dedicated to pickleball — no tennis net at the wrong height, no second set of lines to read through. It is out by the Havelock neighbourhood in north-east Lincoln, open 5:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. The one caveat is a documentation one: the park's own page never mentions pickleball, so the count rests on the City's pickleball page alone.

best_for.heading: Best if you can take what you find
best_for.text: Densmore Park is six courts on the City's own arithmetic — "two dedicated pickleball courts; 2 dual striped (can be used as 4 pickleball courts)". So two are always pickleball and four depend on whether anyone is playing tennis. It is a 61-acre park with ballfields, a basketball court and trails, open 5:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Lincoln have?
faqs.a: More than we can verify. We have confirmed 22 across three City of Lincoln parks: ten at Peterson (Erwin) Park, six at Ballard Park and six at Densmore Park. The City names a fourth park with six dedicated courts, Eden, which is not published here for the reason below, and seven more parks with dual-striped courts it never puts a number to.

faqs.q: Are these real pickleball courts or tennis courts with lines?
faqs.a: Both, and the City tells you which is which. It has a "Dedicated Pickleball Courts" section — Ballard, Eden and Peterson — and a "Dual Striped" section for courts shared with tennis. Sixteen of the 22 courts published here are dedicated, the highest proportion of any city on this site.

faqs.q: How does Densmore add up to six?
faqs.a: The City does the sum itself: "two dedicated pickleball courts; 2 dual striped (can be used as 4 pickleball courts)". Two plus four. We have not multiplied anything — the parenthesis is the City converting its own two tennis courts into a pickleball number, and we publish the sentence on the venue page so you can check the arithmetic.

5:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m., seven days a week, at all three parks, from the Hours block on each park's own page. Lincoln is one of very few operators in this directory that publishes park hours at all, and the only one where every published venue has the same ones.

faqs.q: Who runs play on these courts?
faqs.a: The City says Pickleball Lincoln, Inc. organises and schedules pickleball programming at seven of its parks, including all three published here, and that during those scheduled times the dual-use courts are reserved for pickleball play. It adds that the public is welcome to participate. That is an unusual arrangement to find written down, and it is the closest thing to a peak-times answer any city in this directory publishes.

faqs.q: Are the courts free? Are they lit?
faqs.a: Neither is stated, so neither is published. The City says nothing about the cost of an outdoor court anywhere in Lincoln — it asks you to phone about fees for its indoor courts, which is a different question about four buildings that publish no pickleball count. On lighting there is one near miss worth naming: Densmore Park's page says "Lights: MUSCO (2000). Tournament quality", under a heading describing the four baseball fields the City rents out. Lighting on a ballfield is not lighting on a pickleball court.

Because its address does not resolve, and that is the only reason. Eden has six dedicated courts and is the best-documented venue in the city — it is the one park whose own page lists Pickleball among its features. But the address the City prints for it, "46 Antelope Creek Rd", is found by neither the US Census address file nor OpenStreetMap, and the City's own description of the same park places it "near 46th and Antelope Creek Road" — an intersection rather than a house number. This site does not publish a venue it cannot place on a map. The day that address resolves, or the City prints a different one, six courts join this page.

faqs.q: Why do two of the three venues have a warning on them?
faqs.a: Because the City keeps two records of its own courts and they disagree. The Tennis and Pickleball page counts the pickleball venues; each park also has a page in Parks A to Z with a Features list. At Peterson the two agree. At Ballard and Densmore the park's own page never mentions pickleball at all — its Features list says "Tennis Courts" — so those counts rest on one City page rather than two. Nothing contradicts them and we publish them; we just decline to imply two sources agree when only one has spoken.

faqs.q: How do you know all this?
faqs.a: From the City of Lincoln's own pages, snapshotted on 4 September 2026 and committed to the repository that builds this site, so every number here can be checked against the document it came from. Our build re-reads those snapshots on every run — including the absence of pickleball on two park pages — so a claim on this page cannot quietly stop being true without the build failing.
